chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al-Asamm, from Abdullah Al-Arjani, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while he was eating, and I saw him picking up sesame-seed-sized pieces of food that had fallen from the food-spread. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are picking up this?' He said, 'O Abdullah, this is your sustenance, so do not leave it. Indeed, in it is a healing from every illness.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding food that falls from the table during a meal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the virtue of not wasting sustenance by retrieving even sesame-sized crumbs, identifying them as one's pre-ordained rizq. This practice is linked to spiritual and physical healing, reflecting the Shia emphasis on gratitude (shukr) and mindfulness in daily acts of worship. The narration underscores the belief that every particle of food is divinely allocated, encouraging believers to treat eating as an act of reverence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al Asamma, from Abdullah Al Arjany who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> was eating. So I saw him pursue the likes of the sesame seeds from the food what fell off from the food-spread. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are pursuing this?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abdullah! This is the sustenance, therefore do not leave it, but in it is a healing from every illness’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from certain persons of his people from al- Asamm from ‘ Abd Allah al-Arjaniy who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he was eating. I saw him searching for pieces of food fallen on the table-spread of the size of sesame seed. I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, are you looking for such pieces?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O ‘Abd Allah, it is your sustenance; do not leave them, and besides there is cure in them for all kinds of illness.’”
